units.translation: I see a hawk rushing upon them with wings in its course.
The vision has gone, not later, with wings as attendants (following Dobraeus) along the paths of sleep.
We are caught by our own wings.
He brandishes the wing of a white-rumped hawk.
of the same wing, sharing wings
I will stand as enemy with enemy. Bring quickly greaves, defenses against spear and stones.

the defenses of the spear, that is, the spear, periphrastically, which we hold before us in battle. It is also written 'of wings'. And the reading 'of stones' you might explain thus: the defenses of stones, that is, the shield, which we hold before our body, and by which we receive the showers of stones coming upon us from the enemy. But by 'defenses of wings' understand arrows.
written 'spear', so that it would be thus: bring quickly and speedily the greaves and the spear and, for the sake of the stones, the defenses, that is, the shields.
But if I had my foot on foreign soil, by this well-aimed shaft you would have died, a prey to the image of Zeus's daughter.
he reveres those who are under the wings of Pallas
the varied evils of mortals; nowhere would you see the same wing of toil
wing of murder: the winged or swift one through arrows. But it is better to understand 'murder' periphrastically.
of the same wing, sharing wings
rowing with the oars of wings.
a dappled wing will again encompass him.

which properly signifies a multitude of feathers, or the feathery covering of birds, as τρίχωμα [hair] is said of a hairy covering; of arrows, as elsewhere πτερόν [wing], Aeschylus used it in fr. 129: πληγέντ᾽ ἀτράκτῳ τοξικῷ τὸν ἀετὸν εἰπεῖν ἰδόντα μηχανὴν πτερώματος [struck by a bow-sped shaft, the eagle said, seeing the contrivance of the feathering]
about which the scholiast on Aristophanes' Birds 808 says: πεποίηκεν ὁ Αἰσχύλος ἀετὸν τρωννύ [Aeschylus has made an eagle ...]
struck by a bow-sped shaft, the eagle said, seeing the contrivance of the feathering
Birds 808: Aeschylus has made an eagle ...
I rushed forth unshod on a winged chariot.
We will not give you up to the snatchings of winged creatures.
But the winged hound of Zeus, the blood-red eagle.
about eagles: with the winged hounds of the father.
winged (πτηνά M, but with a superscript) and land-walking creatures.
having seized a winged, white-shining serpent.
I accurately distinguished the flight of hook-clawed birds.
to cower, to crouch in fear
and never cowering before harsh threats.
to be terrified, to be agitated
to be dismayed, to be terrified
She cried out from sleep, terrified.
